subject: SteadyCrest sizing + latency runway — post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@shipwise.io>, Priya Nair <priya@shipwise.io>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: SteadyCrest sizing + latency runway — post-demo clarifications

Thanks again for taking the demo today — nice walkthrough of the Live Fulfillment flow. Quick recap and a few asks so our SRE/benchmarking team can size an appropriate trial. Please confirm the three bullets below or correct any numbers: 

- Latency SLOs: you indicated a 95th percentile (p95) latency target of ~220ms for non-streaming prediction endpoints and p95 <= 350ms for streaming websockets when session length <= 30s. Is that correct?
- Throughput / tokens: the call mentioned typical steady-state is ~180 QPS across the fleet (~6.5k tokens/s aggregate), with peak crest windows hitting ~1,200 QPS for short bursts (1-3m). Please confirm average tokens per request (you said ~36 tokens) and peak tokens per request (you said up to ~420 for multi-step retrievals).
- Concurrency & sessions: are concurrent open streaming sessions expected to top out at ~600 connections during morning peak, with median session duration ~22s? Also confirm whether long-lived sessions (>=2m) are <2% of traffic.

I've attached the anonymized workload CSV you shared in the call (shipwise_workload_sample.csv) and a preliminary SLO-proposal-v1.pdf that maps those numbers to three trial capacity profiles (pilot / burst / enterprise).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm numbers above (reply inline) so I can hand-off to performance for a tailored bench.
- If confirmed, Jordan will run a 24-hr synthetic run against a mirrored dataset next week and share token/QPS traces.
- Schedule a short alignment with engineering on Thursday (30 mins) to agree on connection timeouts and backpressure behavior for streaming.

Thanks — I captured these as action items in the body below for clarity.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
attachments: shipwise_workload_sample.csv (csv, 48KB), SLO-proposal-v1.pdf (pdf, 250KB)
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@shipwise.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@shipwise.io>
Date: 2027-04-11T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SteadyCrest sizing + latency runway — post-demo clarifications

Thanks, Soojin — helpful recap. Inline answers below.

On 2027-04-11 15:02, Soojin Lee wrote:
> - Latency SLOs: p95 non-streaming ~220ms; p95 streaming <=350ms when session <=30s.
This matches what we need in production. We can be flexible on streaming p95 up to 400ms for the pilot, as long as sustained peaks don't drift past that for more than 5 minutes.

> - Throughput / tokens: steady-state ~180 QPS (~6.5k tokens/s), peaks ~1,200 QPS (1-3m bursts). avg tokens/request ~36; peak tokens/request up to ~420.
Avg tokens ~34 (we rounded earlier), peak tokens/request can be 480 for a few complex fulfillment threads. I'll attach a short export of session histograms to the Drive folder.

> - Concurrency & sessions: concurrent streaming sessions ~600 at morning peak; median duration ~22s; long-lived sessions >=2m <2%
Morning peak concurrency is correct; long-lived sessions are closer to 1.1% historically. One caveat: on promo days concurrent sessions have a secondary crest (~150 extra connections) for ~10–20 minutes.

Also: procurement timeline — we plan to finish vendor review by end of May. For the trial we would ask for a reserved pilot window with up to 1.5x the pilot capacity if we validate steady-state behavior during the first 48 hours.

Link to our perf export: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cShipWiseLoadTests

I'm happy to sync Thurs 4/15 at 10:00am PT — Priya will confirm.

— Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering, ShipWise

Subject: Re: SteadyCrest sizing + latency runway — post-demo clarifications

Appreciate the quick answers and the Drive link — that helps a lot. Confirming actions and owners below: 

1) Performance bench (Jordan) — mirror the CSV and run 24-hour synthetic with two profiles: Pilot (180 QPS steady, 1,200 QPS crest) and Burst (360 QPS steady, 1,800 QPS crest). Deliverables: percentile latency traces, token/sec traces, and connection drop/retry counts. ETA: Wed 4/20.
2) Streaming behavior doc (Marcus) — capture timeouts, per-connection backpressure rules, and recommended client retry window. ETA: Tue 4/19.
3) Procurement & trial sizing (Soojin) — I'll draft the pilot reservation ask (1 month, adjustable to 1.5x pilot capacity if validated). Send a short MOU template by EOD 4/13.

Question for you: for the 24-hr run, can you provide a small sample of real request IDs we can use to seed similarity in token distribution (5–10 request IDs)? If not, Jordan will rely on the histograms in the Drive.

If that plan looks good I'll book Thurs 4/15 10:00am PT for the alignment call and loop in Performance Slack channel once the bench starts.

Thanks — looking forward to the trial.

— Soojin
